headline: New techniques and frameworks emerge for building more resilient and efficient AI applications
tldr: Today's AI news highlights the importance of understanding different techniques for training AI models and building local-first applications. Two articles from Towards Data Science discuss the use of RAG vs fine-tuning and orchestrating multiple agents with Claude Code. Meanwhile, InfoQ AI/ML explores the AT Protocol for building more resilient local-first applications. These advancements have significant implications for the development of more efficient and robust AI systems.

research.title: RAG vs Fine-Tuning Explained: What They Actually Do and When to Use Each
research.summary: This article explains the differences between RAG and fine-tuning techniques for training AI models, highlighting their respective use cases.
research.why_it_matters: Understanding the strengths and weaknesses of different training techniques is crucial for developing effective AI models.

features_updates.title: How to Orchestrate 100+ Agents With Claude Code
features_updates.summary: This article demonstrates how to use Claude Code to orchestrate multiple agents in parallel, enabling more efficient and scalable AI applications.
features_updates.why_it_matters: The ability to orchestrate multiple agents is essential for building complex AI systems that can handle large amounts of data and tasks.

top_story.title: How to Build More Resilient Local-First Applications With AT Protocol Infrastructure
top_story.summary: This article discusses the AT Protocol as a framework for building local-first applications, emphasizing the importance of a local-first architecture for data synchronization and updates.
top_story.why_it_matters: The development of local-first applications has significant implications for data ownership, security, and the future of distributed systems.
